title: Weekly Dose of Optimism #219
gist: Packy McCormick's weekly optimism roundup: DeepMind's AlphaGenome 2 nearly doubles causal-variant detection (16% to 30%), argenx buys macrocycle developer Unnatural Products for up to $1.15B, Path Robotics raises $300M at $2.45B for adaptive robot welders, SpaceX orders HJT solar lines from SINGULUS targeting 100 GW (which he flags as preposterous and bubble-like), and LSD reverses brain-aging gene signatures in rodents; it also reports Jensen Huang's resignation from Nvidia.

insights.claim: Google DeepMind's AlphaGenome 2 extends AlphaGenome 1 (1 million DNA letters, tissue-averaged predictions) by adding a condition input — tissue, cell type, cell state, or a few dozen unseen user cells — and species, predicting DNA function in that specific context.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Context-specific genomic prediction is a new capability layer for target discovery; watch Google's bio-AI lead vs. LLM-only labs.

insights.claim: AlphaGenome 2 was trained on more than 107 million individual cell profiles from 68 human and mouse tissues, and on a 28-immune-cell-type benchmark it identified 30% of believed-causal variants versus 16% for AlphaGenome 1.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Near-doubling of causal-variant recall in one generation signals rapid model progress useful for genetics-driven drug discovery.
insights.quote: On a benchmark of 28 immune cell types, it found 30% of the variants scientists believe are causal, versus 16% for the old model.

insights.claim: Genetics has turned into drugs slower than hoped because most GWAS-linked disease variants still require costly real-world experimentation to determine which gene or cell they act on; computational models like AlphaGenome 2 could let researchers screen these variants much faster.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: The bottleneck between cheap genome sequencing and new drugs is variant interpretation — AI that solves it compresses discovery timelines.
insights.locator: Genome-wide association studies have handed us

insights.claim: Packy McCormick frames Google as well positioned: as Nvidia was in turmoil, Google — maker of rival TPUs and a leader in non-LLM scientific models — shipped AlphaGenome 2.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Google's dual position in AI chips (TPUs) and scientific AI is a relative strength vs. Nvidia amid leadership disruption.
insights.quote: So, uhhh, pretty good time to be Google, huh?

insights.claim: The article reports that Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang resigned after two affairs emerged — one with an alleged Chinese spy and one with a direct report — with sources saying more damaging revelations will follow.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: CEO departure at the AI chip leader is a key-person and governance risk; watch succession and further disclosures.
insights.quote: Sources say the affairs are the tip of the iceberg and that heavier shoes will drop.

themes.theme: Macrocycle drug M&A: Argenx buys Unnatural Products

insights.claim: Argenx agreed to acquire Unnatural Products, a not boring capital portfolio company, for $550 million cash upfront plus up to $595 million in development and regulatory milestones (up to $1.15B total).
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Big pharma-adjacent buyers are paying up for oral peptide/macrocycle platforms; comparable valuation marker for the space.

insights.claim: Macrocycles — ring-shaped peptides between pill-form small molecules and injected antibodies — promise biologic-level precision in an oral drug that can enter cells to hit targets antibodies cannot reach, e.g. an oral GLP-1 or cancer therapeutic.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Oral biologic-like drugs could expand addressable markets for injectable franchises; macrocycle platforms are the enabling modality.
insights.quote: The promise is the precision of a biologic in a pill that can slip inside cells to hit targets antibodies can't reach.
insights.locator: Real bad time to be a disease

insights.claim: Argenx and Unnatural Products have partnered since last year on an oral pill against FcRn, the same target as argenx's Vyvgart, which did $1.72 billion in sales last quarter; argenx was already an investor and UNP's Santa Cruz team will become argenx's peptide discovery hub.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: An oral FcRn drug could extend and defend Vyvgart's franchise; the deal is lifecycle management for argenx's core asset.
insights.locator: argenx and UNP have been partners

themes.theme: Robotic welding and the industrial labor bottleneck

insights.claim: Skilled welders are scarce and highly valuable — top 'golden gloves' welders can earn about $1 million a year — and shipbuilding expansions like Anduril's $3.7 billion Arsenal-2 shipyard will require many more welders than exist.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Skilled-trade scarcity is a binding constraint on US reindustrialization and shipbuilding, creating demand for automation.

insights.claim: Path Robotics' Obsidian model differs from conventional welding robots that repeat programmed paths: it inspects each actual joint, plans a custom weld and adjusts in real time, aiming to match top human welders on variable parts.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Perception-driven adaptive robotics unlocks tasks that classic industrial automation could not handle.
insights.locator: Path Robotics, which brothers Andy and Alex

insights.claim: Path Robotics raised a $300 million Series E led by Georgian at a $2.45 billion valuation, with revenue up 17x in 18 months and customers including Lockheed Martin, Saronic and HII, with which it signed a $600 million deal earlier this year.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Defense/shipbuilding demand is driving hypergrowth in industrial robotics; watch defense primes as anchor customers.
insights.quote: Its revenue is up 17x in 18 months
insights.locator: On Tuesday, Path announced a $300 million

insights.claim: Path Robotics also offers Rove, a welding-enabled Boston Dynamics quadruped with 50 preorders, slated for shipyards and construction sites next year.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Mobile robots extend automated welding to unstructured field sites beyond the factory floor.
insights.locator: They also make a robot dog that welds

themes.theme: SpaceX vertical integration and space-solar ambition

insights.claim: SpaceX signed a contract with German equipment maker SINGULUS for a turnkey heterojunction (HJT) solar cell production line worth a little over €60 million, delivering in 1H 2027 to its Bastrop, Texas satellite factory, with plans to scale to more than 100 GW of production equipment.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Watch SINGULUS and HJT equipment suppliers for follow-on orders; SpaceX entering solar cell manufacturing at scale.

insights.claim: 100 GW per year of solar cells would supply roughly 475,000 Starmind satellites (each with a 75-meter wingspan and 210 kW array) annually, versus about 15,000 active satellites in orbit today — a number the author calls preposterous.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Treat headline capacity targets skeptically; actual committed spend is ~€60M.
insights.quote: That, to be clear, is a preposterous number.
insights.locator: That, to be clear, is a preposterous number

insights.claim: The author argues the €60 million SINGULUS commitment's announcement was likely worth far more than €60 million to SpaceX's (SPCX) market cap by making Starmind look serious, and that promising 475,000 space data centers a year is the kind of claim taken seriously in a bubble.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Signal of bubble-like dynamics in AI/space valuations: announcements outpacing committed capital.
insights.quote: A promise to build 475,000 space data centers a year is also exactly the kind of thing you’d expect to hear - and for people to take at least somewhat seriously - if we were in a bubble.
insights.locator: On the other hand, as it stands

insights.claim: Elon Musk's strategy is full vertical integration — Starmind space data centers launched on Starship, possibly with Terafab chips, currently in partnership with Nvidia, powered by solar — and even if the space plans fall short, extra SpaceX solar capacity would yield cheaper clean energy for consumers.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Vertical integration across launch, compute and power is SpaceX's moat thesis; downside case still adds solar supply.

insights.claim: A study in Aging Cell by Aurora Savino, Francesco Iorio and colleagues mapped age-related gene-expression drift across 3,086 human prefrontal cortex samples (ages two days to 106 years) and found LSD opposed the aging signature in rats and mice more strongly than exercise or an enriched environment, outranking all 193 drugs in a reference database.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Early preclinical signal for psychedelics as neurodegeneration/longevity therapeutics; watch psychedelic biotech pipelines.
insights.locator: Now, in a new study in Aging Cell

insights.claim: In the same research, MDMA and alcohol pushed brain gene expression toward an older profile, while LSD repaired amyloid-β-damaged mouse neurons in a dish, restoring branches and synaptic proteins; the author stresses rodent results do not guarantee human efficacy.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Alzheimer's-relevant mechanism data is early but could fuel interest in psychedelic-based CNS drug development.
insights.locator: MDMA and alcohol had the opposite effect

insights.claim: Voyager 1, launched in 1977, will pass one light-day from Earth 49 years into its journey — the farthest any human-made object has traveled — yet that is only about one 34-trillionth of the way across the 93-billion-light-year observable universe.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Low investor relevance; underscores long-duration engineering durability and the scale of space ambitions.
